description: Use this when a user asks what households pay for electricity or natural gas per kWh in Brazil, the EU, Norway and Iceland or the United States, how that compares with another country, or how it changed since the previous period. Returns the official average price per kWh for a standard household consumption band, for the latest period published, with the same band excluding VAT and excluding all taxes, every band, the previous period and the change, and the official source and licence. This is a published average (price_type official_statistic), not a range built from sales, so the range fields are null and there is no sample size. How fresh: Brazil: updated whenever ANEEL homologates a tariff adjustment (each distributor adjusts once a year); each answer states the validity period of the tariff; the EU, Norway and Iceland: updated twice a year (half-yearly figures); each answer states its reference period, and the newest half-year Eurostat holds for the country is returned; the United States: monthly: EIA adds a month to each table about two months after it ends (electricity in the last week of the month, natural gas at the month's end); our copy is refreshed daily and each answer states its month. Do not use for business or industrial tariffs, for a specific supplier's offer or a quote for a particular home, for petrol and diesel, or for other countries.

consumption_band.description: Standard household consumption band, by letter or by the publisher's code (the country notes list them). Leave out for the standard band. BR: not used (one residential tariff per distributor). EU/NO/IS, annual consumption. Electricity: ALL = all consumption bands together; DA = under 1,000 kWh a year; DB = 1,000 to 2,499 kWh a year; DC = 2,500 to 4,999 kWh a year; DD = 5,000 to 14,999 kWh a year; DE = 15,000 kWh a year or more; default DC. Gas: ALL = all consumption bands together; D1 = under 20 GJ a year (under about 5,600 kWh); D2 = 20 to 199 GJ a year (about 5,600 to 55,000 kWh); D3 = 200 GJ a year or more (about 55,600 kWh and over); default D2. ALL = all bands together. Eurostat codes such as KWH2500-4999 or GJ20-199 also work. US: not used (EIA publishes one average for all residential customers in a state).

country.description: BR = Brazil (ANEEL: regulated residential electricity tariff per distributor, R$ per kWh before taxes); EU member states plus NO and IS, as ISO codes (GR for Greece): AT = Austria, BE = Belgium, BG = Bulgaria, HR = Croatia, CY = Cyprus, CZ = Czechia, DK = Denmark, EE = Estonia, FI = Finland, FR = France, DE = Germany, GR = Greece, HU = Hungary, IE = Ireland, IT = Italy, LV = Latvia, LT = Lithuania, LU = Luxembourg, MT = Malta, NL = Netherlands, PL = Poland, PT = Portugal, RO = Romania, SK = Slovakia, SI = Slovenia, ES = Spain, SE = Sweden, NO = Norway, IS = Iceland; US = United States (U.S. Energy Information Administration: average residential electricity price in cents per kWh and residential natural gas price in US$ per thousand cubic feet, by state, monthly)

distributor.description: BR only: the electricity distributor by ANEEL short name, for example 'CEMIG-D', 'ENEL SP', 'LIGHT', 'COPEL-DIS'. Leave out for the median of all distributors.

energy.description: electricity or gas (natural gas). BR: electricity only (no gas). The figure is the regulated residential tariff (TE energy + TUSD network) before taxes and flag surcharges, as a posted price. EU/NO/IS: Eurostat currently has no recent household gas price for CY, FI, IS, MT or NO (status no_matches). US: electricity = average residential price in US cents per kWh (Electric Power Monthly); gas = average residential natural gas price in US dollars per thousand cubic feet (Natural Gas Monthly). EIA gives gas per Mcf, not per kWh, so the two cannot be compared directly.

state.description: US only: the state, by name or postal code ('Texas', 'TX', 'DC'). Leave out for the U.S. average. Gas: EIA publishes no figure for a few states in recent months, then the newest published month is returned and the answer says so.

taxes.description: Tax level of the price. 'all' = all taxes and levies included (what a household pays, default); 'excl_vat' = excluding VAT and other recoverable taxes; 'none' = excluding all taxes and levies. BR: not used. ANEEL tariffs are always before taxes (ICMS, PIS/COFINS) and flag surcharges. US: not used (EIA publishes one average per state).

name: pricepaid_energy_prices

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.
